title: Nightshift knotboard standup - Apr 11 2027
body:
Purpose: quick nightshift standup notes captured on the knotboard — informal, tactical, and action-oriented. Use these for morning handoff; not a canonical postmortem.

TL;DR:
- Two noisy issues surfaced during late-night traffic window; neither currently escalated to SEV1 but both elevated risk to embeddings SLO.
- Autoscale flapping in us-west: transient GPU pool churn caused brief request drops (~30s), mitigated by temporary scaling policy tweak.
- Embedding-store GC pause pattern observed causing tail-latency spikes; on-call patched a hotfix config and queued infra rollback plan if regression continues.

Incidents (timeline/high level):
1) embedding-store tail spikes (2027-04-11 00:42–01:10 UTC)
   - Symptom: 99th-percentile embedding lookups jumped from ~22ms to 1.4s for ~28 minutes, correlated with background GC cycles on node group emb-store-2.
   - Mitigation: rolled out a conservative GC config (lower max-pause target) to nodes in the pool; applied prefix-cache warming for most active keys.
   - Current status: partial mitigation applied, 99p reduced to ~180ms but not back to baseline. Monitoring alert remains in watch mode.
   - Next step: schedule controlled canary of alternate emb-store image with backported jemalloc tuning (JIRA-1248).

2) us-west autoscale jitter (2027-04-11 02:15–02:48 UTC)
   - Symptom: k8s HPA scaled down then up repeatedly during a short capacity oscillation; caused ~120 dropped requests during one 30s window where fallback routing didn't engage fast enough.
   - Root-cause hypothesis: competing autoscaler signals from custom batching controller + noisy CPU metric spike from a load-test-synthetic job.
   - Mitigation: bumped HPA stabilization window to 90s and added a temporary gating flag to batching controller to ignore synthetic-job namespace metrics.
   - Current status: stabilization reduced oscillation; need infra change to rate-limit synthetic load (JIRA-1253).

SLO snapshot (as-of 2027-04-11 03:00 UTC):
- Inference P99 latency (prod-global) vs SLO 300ms: 99.96% OK; small uptick in tails overnight, monitoring.
- Embeddings availability (SLO target 99.9%): 99.82% last 24h (risk zone).
- Error budget: embeddings error budget consumption at 48% for the current 28d window. If we see another day like today, we risk crossing the threshold.

On-call handoff notes (for morning shift):
- Outgoing: Jonah Kim (night) — handing to Diego Morales (day)
- Key open items for next shift:
  * Continue watch on embedding-store GC after canary deploy. If 99p > 300ms for 2 hours, trigger rollback and open SEV channel.
  * Confirm synthetic load throttling (infra) and remove gating flag after proof.
  * Follow up with Applied ML on embedding access patterns; consider LRU window tweak (meet scheduled in calendar).
- Escalation path reminder: first pager -> on-call SRE -> duty manager -> Eng Platform -> Eng Applied ML. Explicit contact list in runbook updated (see PR link).

Runbook updates / immediate doc changes:
- Minor: add GC tuning checklist to emb-store runbook (done, draft PR referenced).
- Minor: document temporary HPA stabilization policy with revert steps (ACTION: Diego to formalize in runbook by EOD).

Action items (owners & expected dates):
- Diego: Draft HPA stabilization revert doc and coordinate synthetic-load rate-limit (target: 2027-04-12). Linked: JIRA-1253.
- Aisha: Lead emb-store canary with jemalloc patch; run two controlled canaries during low-traffic windows and report perf delta (target: 2027-04-13). Linked: JIRA-1248, PR-412.
- Jonah: Compile a short tail-latency playbook (2 pages) for on-call responders; include sample kibana queries and mitigation checklist (target: 2027-04-12 morning).
- Lena (me): Draft post-incident note and schedule follow-up sync with Applied ML and Platform (target: 2027-04-14).

Observations / learnings (free-form):
- The embedding workload is sensitive to small runtime memory pressure events; prefix caching helps but masks rather than solves root cause.
- Our autoscale policy is tuned for aggressive responsiveness; that helps throughput but makes us vulnerable to synthetic or noisy metric bursts. Need a production-safe damping strategy.
- Night ops found the gating flag useful as a temporary lever; consider a safer config toggle for future experiments.

Open questions / discussion prompts for retro:
- Do we want to add a secondary signal to HPA (e.g., queue-length) to avoid noisy CPU-only scaling? Pros/cons?
- How quickly can Applied ML propose model-side mitigation (e.g., smaller embedding shard lookups, batched retrieval)?

Appendix (quick links & snippets):
- Trending dashboards: /dashboards/embeddings-tail-latency (internal)
- Pager thread (Slack): https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C03SRETHREAD/p1654
- JIRA: JIRA-1248 (embedding GC canary), JIRA-1253 (autoscale stabilization)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/412 (jemalloc backport)

Notes to morning lead: skim the top TL;DR, check the embedding 99p widget, and ping Applied ML on the scheduled sync. If anything looks worse than outlined, escalate immediately.

-- Lena
